messages:
Ana V.: FYI customer reported SDK failing in Next.js middleware build: error 'crypto.subtle is not a function' and TypeScript can't find fetch/crypto types.

Theo M.: Likely the Node bundle is being picked by the edge bundler. We need conditional exports and an edge-specific ESM build.

Ana V.: Quick repro: importing the package normally resolved to dist/node and pulled in node:crypto -> bundler shim breaks subtle. Dynamic import of dist/edge fixed it.

Theo M.: Plan: add exports map so importers in ESM/edge pick dist/edge/index.mjs. Also ship dist/edge/index.d.ts that references DOM libs so users don't have to modify tsconfig. Example exports block for package.json: {"import":"./dist/edge/index.mjs","require":"./dist/node/index.cjs"}.

Ana V.: Also we should avoid using response.clone() in retry logic for edge builds; middleware runtimes have different stream semantics. Add an edgeRetryMode that buffers small bodies instead of cloning.

Theo M.: For crypto, create platform abstraction src/platform/crypto.ts with two implementations. Build pipeline aliases node->node-impl, edge->webcrypto-impl. That prevents accidental node imports in edge bundle.

ops-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/501 "Edge: exports + types + runtime-safe implementations" and assigned to @theo.

Ana V.: I'll add a docs FAQ entry with a tiny middleware example and the dynamic-import workaround for users until a release lands.

Theo M.: I'll prototype the dist/edge build and add a minimal Next.js example in the repo for CI `next build` smoke tests.

Ana V.: Thanks, that should reduce onboarding friction for Next middleware users.
